headline: MYANMAR PITCHES US ON RARE EARTHS ACCESS — MILITARY GOVT TARGETS WESTERN CAPITAL TO BREAK CHINA'S GRIP
snippet: Myanmar's military government is urging Washington to rapidly expand investment in its rare earth mining sector, which China currently dominates as a processing partner — a geopolitically charged offer given ongoing Western sanctions over the 2021 coup. The pitch arrives the same day China's two-month rare earth export waiver extension takes effect, underscoring the fragility of Western buyers' supply security without diversified non-Chinese sources.

headline: PENTAGON PUTS $2 BILLION INTO CRITICAL MINERALS STOCKPILE — RARE EARTHS, TUNGSTEN, VANADIUM IN 19 PACKAGES
snippet: The US Defense Logistics Agency committed $2 billion in fiscal year 2026 to acquire critical materials — including rare earths, tungsten, titanium, vanadium and antimony — for the National Defense Stockpile under 19 rapid acquisition packages covering more than 30 materials. The commitment creates a government demand anchor that reduces offtake risk for domestic producers in targeted sectors and signals sustained federal purchasing through 2027.

headline: MCEWEN Q3 "QUARTER OF TRANSITION" — NEW RAVEN ZONE FOUND AT GREY FOX, EXPLORATION SPEND +65% TO $11.2M
snippet: McEwen Mining (TSX/NYSE: MUX) labeled Q3 2026 a "Quarter of Transition," revealing a newly discovered Raven Zone within its Grey Fox gold deposit in Ontario alongside a 65% year-over-year surge in exploration spending to $11.2 million. The Raven Zone adds resource-growth optionality to a deposit whose June 2026 prefeasibility study already projects 100,000+ oz/yr gold production by 2029 — a catalyst the market hasn't yet priced at $4,100+ gold.

headline: AMERICAN RARE EARTHS FIRES UP WYOMING HALLECK CREEK PRODUCTION TEST — OXIDE + METALS FOR US MAGNETS
snippet: ASX-listed American Rare Earths (ASX: ARR) has begun small-scale continuous ore processing from its Halleck Creek project in Wyoming under an MOU with Novex, aiming to produce rare earth oxides and metals for a domestic US magnet supply chain. The Wyoming-based test program targets a critical gap in domestic rare earth supply: separation and metal production capacity that currently sits almost entirely in China — a different US rare earth development play from USAR's Texas/Brazil assets.

headline: GOLD MINERS RALLIED WHILE GOLD FELL — RADOMSKI WARNS IT'S STOCKS DRAGGING MINERS UP, NOT METAL: $3,500 TARGET
snippet: Analyst Przemek Radomski flagged an ominous market dynamic on November 9: GDX and GDXJ rose as gold fell on CPI data because the miner ETFs were carried by the broad stock market rally, not metal demand — a warning that miners are following equities rather than the metal. With GDXJ near $111.70 and December gold futures near $4,125, Radomski's bear case is that when stocks reverse, miners fall harder than gold toward a $3,500 target.

headline: ACG METALS ACQUIRES FULLY PERMITTED NUSSIR ARCTIC COPPER MINE FOR $220M — NORWAY PRODUCTION TARGET H1 2028
snippet: ACG Metals agreed to acquire 100% of Blue Moon Norway — including the construction-stage Nussir copper mine and Ulveryggen project — from Blue Moon Metals (TSX-V: MOON) for US$220 million in shares, creating a focused European copper company with a fully permitted Arctic Norwegian project targeting first copper concentrate in H1 2028. The deal provides a live transaction benchmark for construction-ready copper assets globally: $220M for 94.52% of a permitted, under-construction mine in a stable jurisdiction.

headline: IVANHOE MINES SLASHES KAMOA-KAKULA TARGET AGAIN — 2027 OUTPUT CUT 25% TO 300-350KT AS COSTS SOAR
snippet: Ivanhoe Mines delivered its second Kamoa-Kakula production downgrade of 2026, cutting its 2027 copper output target approximately 25% to 300,000–350,000 tonnes (from 380,000–420,000) while raising cash cost guidance to $2.50–$3.00/lb as stoping delays and lower grades hit the DRC flagship. TD Securities and Stifel both downgraded Ivanhoe to Hold; the stock is down 47% year-to-date, illustrating how execution risk reprices even large-scale copper producers despite tight physical supply.

headline: BARRANCO GOLD MINING LAUNCHES $3M FLOW-THROUGH FOR KING PROPERTY — BC NICOLA-SIMILKAMEEN BELT
snippet: CSE-listed Barranco Gold Mining (CSE: BAR) announced a flow-through share offering of up to $3 million to fund exploration on the King Property in BC's Nicola and Similkameen Mining Divisions — a district hosting numerous copper-gold porphyry and epithermal gold prospects in one of Canada's most prolific mining corridors. The raise signals continued early-stage exploration activity in BC at current gold prices despite subdued junior financing markets.

headline: ZAMBIA BETS ON DOWNSTREAM EV AND BATTERY PRODUCTION — COPPER-COBALT BELT TARGETS VALUE-ADD PLAY
snippet: Zambia is actively courting investment in domestic EV assembly and battery manufacturing, aiming to capture downstream value from its position as a major copper and cobalt producer rather than exporting raw concentrate — mirroring strategies by Indonesia (nickel) and Chile (copper). The pitch aligns with growing Western demand for locally processed battery materials, though Zambia has yet to announce specific plant capacity or confirmed partner commitments.

headline: WHY COPPER AND URANIUM STOCKS OUTPERFORM IN A SOFT ECONOMY — 4 STRUCTURAL DRIVERS EXPLAINED
snippet: Discovery Alert's November 2026 analysis unpacks why copper and uranium equities have outperformed broader markets during the economic slowdown: non-discretionary demand (uranium for nuclear baseload; copper for AI-driven grid build-out), constrained mine supply pipelines, geopolitical supply-chain rewiring away from China, and government-mandated stockpiling creating a persistent demand floor. For TSX-V and ASX junior investors, the piece frames why commodity-specific structural drivers can decouple from macro sentiment — and which projects benefit most.
